mine.lesson.first_steps.title: First steps with Byte
mine.lesson.first_steps.reflection: Why is it useful to save instructions in a program instead of typing them one at a time?
mine.lesson.first_steps.hello.goal: In Byte's terminal, first type edit hello to start the program; in it, make your Byte say something in chat with mine.say, then save and run it.
mine.lesson.first_steps.hello.not_yet: Not yet: your program has to make Byte speak with mine.say.
mine.lesson.first_steps.hello.hint.1: Check that the terminal's line starts with > and not with lua> (type exit() to leave lua), then type edit hello.
mine.lesson.first_steps.hello.hint.2: In the editor write mine.say("Hi!"). Press Ctrl, pick Save with the arrows and press Enter; then Ctrl again, Exit, Enter. In the terminal type hello and press Enter.
mine.lesson.first_steps.hello.block_goal: Make your Byte say something in chat with the "say" block, then run the program.
mine.lesson.first_steps.hello.block_hint: In Byte group, drag the "say" block into the white area and write something in it.
Press Run ▶ and go back to Minecraft: after 3, 2, 1 your Byte speaks in the chat.
mine.lesson.first_steps.roundtrip.goal: Write a new program (edit roundtrip) that takes Byte 3 blocks forward and back to where it started, facing the same way.
mine.lesson.first_steps.roundtrip.not_ye: Not yet: Byte has to go at least 3 blocks away and come back to where it started, facing the same way.
mine.lesson.first_steps.roundtrip.hint.1: Plan it on paper first: how many steps forward? How many turns to face back?
mine.lesson.first_steps.roundtrip.hint.2: To turn around, turn twice: byte.turnLeft() two times. At the end, turn twice again.
mine.lesson.first_steps.roundtrip.block_: Plan it on paper first: how many steps forward? How many turns to face back?
To turn around, use "turn left" twice. At the end, turn twice again.
mine.lesson.first_steps.tower.goal: Write a new program (edit tower) that builds a tower 3 blocks tall in front of Byte, then brings Byte back down.
mine.lesson.first_steps.tower.not_yet: Not yet: build a tower 3 blocks tall right in front of where Byte started, and bring Byte back down.
mine.lesson.first_steps.tower.hint.1: Byte needs blocks: put at least 3 in the highlighted slot of its 4x4 inventory, all in that same slot.
mine.lesson.first_steps.tower.hint.2: Place a block, go up, place a block... then come back down.
mine.lesson.first_steps.tower.block_hint: Byte needs blocks: put at least 3 in the highlighted slot of its 4x4 inventory, all in that same slot.
"place a block in front", "move up", "place a block in front"... then "move down" until Byte is back on the ground.
mine.lesson.loops.title: Loops: rows, floors and cubes
mine.lesson.loops.reflection: How many lines would the cube take without loops? What would you change in your program to build a cube 10 blocks wide?
mine.lesson.loops.row.goal: Write a program that builds a straight row of 10 blocks, using a for loop.
mine.lesson.loops.row.not_yet: Not yet: build a straight row of 10 blocks, one block high.
mine.lesson.loops.row.hint.1: byte.placeDown() puts a block under Byte, so first go up one block with byte.up(). MINE has already put the blocks in the highlighted slot.
mine.lesson.loops.row.hint.2: for i = 1, 10 do ... end repeats what is inside 10 times. Inside the loop: place a block below, then move forward.
mine.lesson.loops.row.block_goal: Write a program that builds a straight row of 10 blocks, using a repeat block.
mine.lesson.loops.row.block_hint.1: The "place a block below" block puts a block under Byte, so first "move up". MINE has already put the blocks in the highlighted slot.
mine.lesson.loops.row.block_hint.2: "repeat 10 times" repeats the blocks inside it. Inside: "place a block below", then "move forward".
mine.lesson.loops.floor.goal: Build a solid floor 5 blocks long and 4 blocks wide. How many blocks does it take?
mine.lesson.loops.floor.not_yet: Not yet: build a solid floor, 5 blocks long and 4 wide, one block thick.
mine.lesson.loops.floor.hint.1: A floor is 4 rows of 5 blocks: put the loop for one row inside another loop. How many blocks does it take? Area = 5 × 4 = 20.
mine.lesson.loops.floor.hint.2: After each row: go back to the start of the row with byte.back() 5 times (another loop), then turn right, move forward one block and turn left.
mine.lesson.loops.floor.block_hint.1: A floor is 4 rows of 5 blocks: put the "repeat" of one row inside another "repeat". How many blocks does it take? Area = 5 × 4 = 20.
mine.lesson.loops.floor.block_hint.2: After each row, still inside the outer "repeat": "repeat 5 times" "move back", then "turn right", "move forward" and "turn left".
mine.lesson.loops.cube.goal: Build a solid cube 3 blocks long, 3 wide and 3 tall. How many blocks does it take?
mine.lesson.loops.cube.not_yet: Not yet: build a solid cube, 3 × 3 × 3, with no holes.
mine.lesson.loops.cube.hint.1: A cube is 3 floors stacked on top of each other: put your floor inside a third loop. Volume = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 blocks.
mine.lesson.loops.cube.hint.2: Start every layer by going up one block. After a layer, go back to its first row: turn left, move forward 3 blocks, turn right.
mine.lesson.loops.cube.block_hint.1: A cube is 3 floors stacked on top of each other: put your floor inside a third "repeat". Volume = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 blocks.
mine.lesson.loops.cube.block_hint.2: Start every layer with "move up". After a layer, go back to its first row: "turn left", "repeat 3 times" "move forward", "turn right".
mine.lesson.debugging.title: Debugging: fix Byte's programs
mine.lesson.debugging.reflection: Which bug was hardest to find? How did you find it?
mine.lesson.debugging.typo.goal: Your Byte has three new programs. Start with broken_row: run it, read the error, and fix it so that it builds a row of 6 blocks.
mine.lesson.debugging.typo.not_yet: Not yet: the row needs 6 blocks in a straight line. Does broken_row still stop with an error?
mine.lesson.debugging.typo.hint.1: Read the error: the number after the program's name is the line where Lua stopped. Open the program with edit broken_row and go to that line.
mine.lesson.debugging.typo.hint.2: Lua tells capital and small letters apart: compare that line with the instructions you used in the loops lesson.
mine.lesson.debugging.typo.block_goal: MINE has put three broken programs among your programs (the "My programs" menu). Start with broken_row: run it, watch Byte, and fix it so that it builds a row of 6 blocks.
mine.lesson.debugging.typo.block_hint.1: Watch where the block ends up: in front of Byte, in the air. Which block decides where the blocks go?
mine.lesson.debugging.typo.block_hint.2: The place a block block has a menu: in front, above, below. Which one makes a row on the ground?
mine.lesson.debugging.missing_end.goal: Now broken_floor: Lua won't even start it. Fix it so that it builds a floor 4 blocks long and 3 wide.
mine.lesson.debugging.missing_end.not_ye: Not yet: the floor must be 4 blocks long and 3 wide, 12 blocks in all.
mine.lesson.debugging.missing_end.hint.1: The message says "Expected end": something was opened and never closed. Every for needs its own end.
mine.lesson.debugging.missing_end.hint.2: Lua points at line 3, but the missing end belongs to another loop. Which loop isn't closed? The indentation helps.
mine.lesson.debugging.missing_end.block_: Now broken_floor: it builds, but the wrong shape. Fix it so that it builds a floor 4 blocks long and 3 wide.
Read MINE's measurements: the floor is 3 tall, so every row is one block higher than the one before. Which block makes Byte go up?
move up must happen once, before the rows: drag it out of the repeat and put it above it.
mine.lesson.debugging.wrong_size.goal: Last one: broken_square runs without errors, but it should build a square 4 × 4. Run it, look at what it builds, and fix it.
mine.lesson.debugging.wrong_size.not_yet: Not yet: the square must be 4 blocks long and 4 wide, 16 blocks in all.
mine.lesson.debugging.wrong_size.hint.1: No error message this time: compare what Byte built with the goal. How many blocks are in one row?
mine.lesson.debugging.wrong_size.hint.2: Each row has two loops, one going forward and one coming back: they must repeat the same number of times.
mine.lesson.debugging.wrong_size.block_g: Last one: broken_square should build a square 4 × 4. Run it, look at what it builds, and fix it.
mine.lesson.debugging.wrong_size.block_h: Compare what Byte built with the goal: how many blocks are in one row?
Each row has two repeat blocks, one going forward and one coming back: they must repeat the same number of times.
mine.lesson.conditions.title: Conditions: Byte decides
mine.lesson.conditions.reflection: MINE changed the challenge every time, but your programs still worked. How did Byte know what to do?
mine.lesson.conditions.wall.goal: Every time your program starts, MINE builds a wall in front of Byte, at a different distance. Write a program that climbs over the wall and lands right behind it.
mine.lesson.conditions.wall.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to land right behind the wall, back on the ground, without breaking it.
mine.lesson.conditions.wall.hint.1: byte.detect() is true when there is a block in front of Byte. while not byte.detect() do ... end repeats until Byte touches the wall.
mine.lesson.conditions.wall.hint.2: When the loop ends, Byte is touching the wall: go up, forward twice, then down.
mine.lesson.conditions.wall.block_hint.1: The "block in front?" block is true when there is a block in front of Byte. Put "not block in front?" in "repeat while": it repeats until Byte touches the wall.
mine.lesson.conditions.wall.block_hint.2: When the loop ends, Byte is touching the wall: "move up", "move forward" twice, then "move down".
mine.lesson.conditions.gold.goal: Now MINE lays a row of 8 blocks in front of Byte: stone, with some gold in different places every time. Dig up only the gold, and leave the stone.
mine.lesson.conditions.gold.not_yet: Not yet: dig up all the gold in the row, and none of the stone.
mine.lesson.conditions.gold.hint.1: MINE has put a gold block in the highlighted slot: byte.compareDown() is true when the block below is the same as that one.
mine.lesson.conditions.gold.hint.2: Go up one block, then 8 times: move forward, and if byte.compareDown() then dig with byte.digDown().
mine.lesson.conditions.gold.block_hint.1: MINE has put a gold block in the highlighted slot: "block below same as the slot's?" is true when the block below is gold too.
mine.lesson.conditions.gold.block_hint.2: "move up", then "repeat 8 times": "move forward", and an "if" with "block below same as the slot's?" that does "dig below".
mine.lesson.conditions.tower.goal: MINE has put some blocks in the highlighted slot. How many? It doesn't matter! Build a tower in front of Byte with all of them, then bring Byte back to the ground.
mine.lesson.conditions.tower.not_yet: Not yet: the tower must use all the blocks in the highlighted slot, and Byte must come back to the ground.
mine.lesson.conditions.tower.hint.1: byte.place() is false when it can't place a block, for example when the slot is empty. while byte.place() do byte.up() end builds until the blocks run out.
mine.lesson.conditions.tower.hint.2: byte.down() is false when Byte touches the ground. while byte.down() do end brings it all the way down.
The "blocks in the slot" block says how many blocks are left. Use "repeat while" with "blocks in the slot > 0" (the compare block is in Logic): "place a block in front", "move up".
Then "repeat until" with "block below?": "move down". Byte stops when it touches the ground.
mine.lesson.functions.title: Variables and functions
mine.lesson.functions.reflection: In the pyramid, the function square(side) did three different jobs. How many lines did it save you? What else could you build with it?
mine.lesson.functions.count.goal: MINE has built a wall in front of Byte, at a distance you don't know. Write a program that takes Byte up to the wall and makes it say how many steps it took.
mine.lesson.functions.count.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right in front of the wall and say how many steps it took.
mine.lesson.functions.count.hint.1: A variable remembers a number: local steps = 0 at the start, then steps = steps + 1 every time Byte moves forward.
mine.lesson.functions.count.hint.2: Walk with while not byte.detect() do ... end, as in the conditions lesson. At the end: mine.say("I took " .. steps .. " steps").
mine.lesson.functions.count.block_hint.1: In Variables, create a variable steps: "set steps to 0" at the start, then "change steps by 1" every time Byte moves forward.
mine.lesson.functions.count.block_hint.2: Walk with "repeat while" and "not block in front?" in it, as in the conditions lesson. At the end use "say" with "create text with" in it: "I took ", steps, " steps".
mine.lesson.functions.square.goal: Each time your program starts, MINE chooses how big a square it wants: local side = mine.challenge() tells you. Build a solid square floor of that size.
mine.lesson.functions.square.not_yet: Not yet: build a solid square floor as big as mine.challenge() asks.
mine.lesson.functions.square.hint.1: It's the floor of the loops lesson, with side instead of the numbers: for row = 1, side do ... end and for i = 1, side do ... end.
mine.lesson.functions.square.hint.2: To see what MINE asks, make Byte say it: mine.say("Side: " .. side).
mine.lesson.functions.square.block_goal: Each time your program starts, MINE chooses how big a square it wants: the challenge's number block tells you. Build a solid square floor of that size.
It's the floor of the loops lesson: "set side to" with "the challenge's number" in it, then put side in every "repeat" instead of the numbers.
To see what MINE asks, make Byte say it: "say" with "create text with" "Side: " and side in it.
mine.lesson.functions.pyramid.goal: Build a step pyramid: a 5 × 5 square, a 3 × 3 square on top of it, and one block on the very top. Write a function square(side) and use it three times.
mine.lesson.functions.pyramid.not_yet: Not yet: the pyramid is a solid 5 × 5 square, then a 3 × 3 square centred on top of it, then one block on top: 35 blocks.
mine.lesson.functions.pyramid.hint.1: function square(side) ... end gives a name to your square program: then square(5), square(3) and square(1) build the three layers. Make the function bring Byte back to the corner where it started.
mine.lesson.functions.pyramid.hint.2: Between two layers: go up one block, move forward one, turn right, move forward one and turn left. Then the next square is centred.
mine.lesson.functions.pyramid.block_goal: Build a step pyramid: a 5 × 5 square, a 3 × 3 square on top of it, and one block on the very top. Make a function square with a parameter side, and use it three times.
mine.lesson.functions.pyramid.block_hint: In Functions, take "to do something" and call it square; with ⚙ add an input side. Put your square inside: then "square with side" 5, 3 and 1 builds the three layers. Make it bring Byte back to the corner where it started.
Between two layers: "move up", "move forward", "turn right", "move forward", "turn left". Then the next square is centred.

mine.lesson.maze.title: The maze: a hand on the wall
mine.lesson.maze.reflection: Your program got Byte out of mazes it had never seen. Why does keeping a hand on the wall always work? When wouldn't it?
mine.lesson.maze.corridor.goal: MINE has built a winding corridor in front of Byte, different every time, with a gold block at its end. Bring Byte right in front of the gold, walking only along the corridor.
mine.lesson.maze.corridor.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right in front of the gold, without climbing or breaking the walls.
mine.lesson.maze.corridor.hint.1: MINE has put a gold block in the highlighted slot: byte.compare() is true when the block in front is gold. while not byte.compare() do ... end repeats until Byte faces it.
mine.lesson.maze.corridor.hint.2: Inside the loop: if not byte.detect() then go forward; else turn right, and if there's a wall there too (and it isn't the gold), turn left twice.
mine.lesson.maze.corridor.block_hint.1: MINE has put a gold block in the highlighted slot: "block in front same as the slot's?" is true when Byte faces the gold. Use "repeat until" with it.
mine.lesson.maze.corridor.block_hint.2: Inside: an "if" with "not block in front?": "move forward"; else "turn right", and if "block in front?" and not the gold, "turn left" twice.
mine.lesson.maze.maze.goal: Now it's a real maze, with dead ends, and a new one every time. Get Byte out: right in front of the gold, without climbing or digging.
mine.lesson.maze.maze.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right in front of the gold, walking only along the corridors.
mine.lesson.maze.maze.hint.1: Keep your right hand on the wall and you'll get out of any maze like this one: at every step, turn right; while there's a wall in front (that isn't the gold), turn left; then one step forward.
mine.lesson.maze.maze.hint.2: while not byte.compare() do: byte.turnRight(), then while byte.detect() and not byte.compare() do byte.turnLeft() end, then if not byte.compare() then byte.forward() end.
mine.lesson.maze.maze.block_hint.1: Keep your right hand on the wall and you'll get out of any maze like this one: at every step, turn right; while there's a wall in front (that isn't the gold), turn left; then one step forward.
mine.lesson.maze.maze.block_hint.2: "repeat until" the gold: "turn right"; "repeat while" "block in front?" and not the gold: "turn left"; if not the gold: "move forward".
mine.lesson.maze.steps.goal: Get Byte out of a new maze again, and at the gold make it say how many steps it took. Count them with a variable: MINE counts them too.
mine.lesson.maze.steps.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop in front of the gold and say how many steps it took.
mine.lesson.maze.steps.hint.1: Before the loop, local steps = 0. Each time Byte goes forward, steps = steps + 1.
mine.lesson.maze.steps.hint.2: At the end: mine.say("I took " .. steps .. " steps"). The .. joins texts and numbers.
mine.lesson.maze.steps.block_hint.1: In Variables, make a variable "steps". Before the loop, "set steps to 0"; after "move forward", "change steps by 1".
mine.lesson.maze.steps.block_hint.2: At the end, "say" with "create text with": "I took ", steps, " steps".
mine.lesson.check.maze_over: Not yet: Byte went over the walls. In a maze it can only walk along the corridors.
mine.lesson.check.maze_broken: Not yet: Byte broke a wall of the maze. Find the way out without digging.
mine.lesson.check.maze_exit: Not yet: Byte stopped %s blocks from the gold. It has to stop right in front of it.
mine.lesson.check.maze_count: Not yet: Byte took %s steps, but said %s. Count every step with a variable.
mine.lesson.treasure.title: Treasure hunt: coordinates
mine.lesson.treasure.reflection: Byte found treasure it couldn't see, with just some numbers. Where are coordinates like these used in real life (maps, GPS, battleships)? Why did Byte need variables to get home?
mine.lesson.treasure.map.goal: MINE has buried a treasure (a gold block) in the ground near Byte, in a new place every time. mine.challenge() says where: so many blocks forward, then so many to the right. Bring Byte right on top of it.
mine.lesson.treasure.map.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right on top of the treasure.
mine.lesson.treasure.map.hint.1: local forward, right = mine.challenge() puts the two numbers in two variables. mine.say them to see them!
mine.lesson.treasure.map.hint.2: for i = 1, forward do byte.forward() end, then byte.turnRight(), then the same with right.
mine.lesson.treasure.map.block_hint.1: "the challenge's number 1" is how far forward, "the challenge's number 2" how far to the right. Keep them in two variables (Variables, "set ... to").
mine.lesson.treasure.map.block_hint.2: "repeat" with the variable forward in it: "move forward". Then "turn right", and the same with right.
mine.lesson.treasure.dig.goal: Now dig the treasure up (Byte digs the block under it with byte.digDown()) and bring Byte back home, where it started.
mine.lesson.treasure.dig.not_yet: Not yet: dig up the treasure, then bring Byte back where it started.
mine.lesson.treasure.dig.hint.1: Your variables still remember how far Byte went: they are the way home too.
mine.lesson.treasure.dig.hint.2: After byte.digDown(): right times byte.back(), byte.turnLeft(), forward times byte.back().
mine.lesson.treasure.dig.block_hint.1: Your variables still remember how far Byte went: they are the way home too.
mine.lesson.treasure.dig.block_hint.2: After "dig below": "repeat" right times "move back", "turn left", "repeat" forward times "move back".
mine.lesson.treasure.three.goal: Three treasures! mine.challenge() gives 6 numbers: forward and right of the first, of the second, of the third. Dig them all up and come back home. Byte has to remember where it is.
mine.lesson.treasure.three.not_yet: Not yet: dig up all three treasures, then bring Byte back where it started.
mine.lesson.treasure.three.hint.1: Two variables, f and r, say where Byte is (they start at 0). A function goTo(toF, toR) moves Byte there: while f < toF go forward and add 1 to f; while f > toF go back and take 1 away; then the same to the right.
mine.lesson.treasure.three.hint.2: for i = 1, 3 do goTo(mine.challenge(2 * i - 1), mine.challenge(2 * i)) byte.digDown() end, then goTo(0, 0) brings Byte home.
mine.lesson.treasure.three.block_hint.1: Two variables, f and r, say where Byte is (start them at 0). In Functions, make "goTo" with two inputs, toF and toR: "repeat while f < toF": "move forward", "change f by 1"; "repeat while f > toF": "move back", "change f by -1"; then the same to the right.
mine.lesson.treasure.three.block_hint.2: Call goTo with "the challenge's number 1" and "2", then "dig below"; then with 3 and 4, and 5 and 6. Last, goTo 0, 0 brings Byte home.
mine.lesson.check.treasure_where: Not yet: the treasure was %s forward and %s to the right; Byte stopped %s forward and %s to the right.
mine.lesson.check.treasure_left: Not yet: %s of %s treasures are still in the ground. Byte digs one standing right on top of it: byte.digDown().
mine.lesson.check.treasure_home: Not yet: all the treasure is dug up, but Byte isn't home: it's %s forward and %s to the right of where it started.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.title: Python: the connected greenhouse (Pico 2 W)
mine.lesson.greenhouse.reflection: Your greenhouse measured, decided and sent back a summary by itself, over Wi-Fi. Which devices around you work like this (a thermostat, a weather station, a smartwatch)? What data do they send, and to whom?
mine.lesson.greenhouse.average.goal: In Python. The Pico 2 W in the greenhouse sends its temperature over Wi-Fi with the key temperatura (MINE plays it to test). Collect 6 temperatures in a list, then make Byte say their average.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.average.not_yet: Not yet: collect 6 temperatures and make Byte say their average.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.average.hint.1: key, value = mine.device.wait("temperatura") waits for the next temperature. In a for loop of 6, temperatures.append(value).
mine.lesson.greenhouse.average.hint.2: sum(temperatures) / len(temperatures) is the average; round(average, 1) keeps one decimal. Then mine.say("Average: " + str(...)).
mine.lesson.greenhouse.alarm.goal: The alarm: every time a temperature arrives, Byte tells the Pico allarme:1 if it's above 30 degrees, else allarme:0 (the Pico lights its LED). Keep the program listening; MINE plays the temperatures to test it.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.alarm.not_yet: Not yet: for each temperature the Pico must get allarme:1 above 30, allarme:0 otherwise.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.alarm.hint.1: while True: wait for a temperature, then mine.device.send("allarme", 1) or mine.device.send("allarme", 0).
mine.lesson.greenhouse.alarm.hint.2: Above 30 means > 30: at exactly 30 it's still allarme:0.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.report.goal: The report: every 5 temperatures, Byte sends their average back to the Pico as media (for example media:24.6), and starts a new group. Keep the program listening.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.report.not_yet: Not yet: after every 5 temperatures the Pico must get their average as media.
mine.lesson.greenhouse.report.hint.1: Keep the temperatures in a list group; when len(group) == 5, send the average with mine.device.send("media", ...).
mine.lesson.greenhouse.report.hint.2: After sending, group = [] starts a new group of 5.
mine.lesson.check.greenhouse_waiting: Not yet: the program ended before all %s temperatures arrived.
mine.lesson.check.greenhouse_say: Not yet: at the end Byte has to say the average with mine.say.
mine.lesson.check.greenhouse_average: Not yet: the temperatures were %s: their average is %s, and Byte said %s.
mine.lesson.check.greenhouse_alarm: Not yet: the temperature was %s, and Byte told the board allarme:%s. It must be 1 only above %s, else 0.
mine.lesson.check.greenhouse_report: Not yet: after the temperatures %s, Byte told the board media:%s. Their average is %s.
mine.lesson.check.keep_listening_python: Not yet: your program ended before MINE could try it. Keep it listening: while True:
mine.lesson.control.title: Python: automatic control (micro:bit)
mine.lesson.control.reflection: Your greenhouse switched its fan on and off by itself, without flickering. Where else does a machine decide by itself with a threshold (a fridge, a heater, street lights)? Why do they need a gap between on and off?
mine.lesson.control.threshold.goal: In Python. The micro:bit measures the temperature and sends it (temperatura). The lamp behind Byte is the greenhouse's fan: it must be on from 28 degrees up, off below. MINE plays the temperatures to test it.
mine.lesson.control.threshold.not_yet: Not yet: the fan (the lamp behind Byte) must be on from 28 degrees up, and off below.
mine.lesson.control.threshold.hint.1: key, temperature = mine.device.wait("temperatura") inside while True:.
mine.lesson.control.threshold.hint.2: redstone.setOutput("back", temperature >= 28): the comparison is already True or False.
mine.lesson.control.hysteresis.goal: With one threshold, at 27-28 degrees the fan would switch on and off all the time. Hysteresis: on at 28 or more, off at 24 or less, and in between it stays as it was.
mine.lesson.control.hysteresis.not_yet: Not yet: on at 28 or more, off at 24 or less, and in between the fan stays as it was.
mine.lesson.control.hysteresis.hint.1: A variable remembers whether the fan is on (on = False before the loop): the program needs a memory.
mine.lesson.control.hysteresis.hint.2: if temperature >= 28: on = True, elif temperature <= 24: on = False, and nothing in between; then redstone.setOutput("back", on).
mine.lesson.control.manual.goal: The gardener's button: button A on the micro:bit (pulsante_a) switches manual mode on and off. In manual mode the fan is always on; in automatic mode it works as before.
mine.lesson.control.manual.not_yet: Not yet: button A switches manual mode (fan always on) on and off; otherwise the fan works as in step 2.
mine.lesson.control.manual.hint.1: key, value = mine.device.wait() with no key waits for anything from the board: look at key to know what arrived.
mine.lesson.control.manual.hint.2: if key == "pulsante_a": manual = not manual. At the end of each turn: redstone.setOutput("back", on or manual).
mine.lesson.check.control_fan: Not yet: after %s the fan should be %s, and it was %s.
mine.lesson.crossing.title: Python: the level crossing (Arduino)
mine.lesson.crossing.reflection: Your crossing was always in one state, and events moved it from one to the other. Which machines around you work like this (a lift, a vending machine, a traffic light)? What are their states and their events?
mine.lesson.crossing.close.goal: In Python. A level crossing: the door in front of Byte is the barrier (open while Byte sends it redstone), the lamp behind it the light. When the program starts the crossing is open and the light off; when the Arduino says a train is coming (treno:1), it closes and the light goes on. MINE plays the Arduino to test it.
mine.lesson.crossing.close.not_yet: Not yet: open with the light off when the program starts; closed with the light on when treno:1 arrives.
mine.lesson.crossing.close.hint.1: A function crossing(closed) does both: redstone.setOutput("front", not closed) and redstone.setOutput("back", closed).
mine.lesson.crossing.close.hint.2: crossing(False) at the start; then while True: mine.device.wait("treno") and crossing(True).
mine.lesson.crossing.reopen.goal: When the train has passed, a sensor on the track (the lever on Byte's left) opens the crossing again. Now there are two kinds of events: a train from the Arduino, a redstone change. Wait for whichever comes first.
mine.lesson.crossing.reopen.not_yet: Not yet: a train closes the crossing (light on), the lever on Byte's left opens it again (light off).
mine.lesson.crossing.reopen.hint.1: event = os.pullEvent() waits for anything: event[0] is "mine_device" for the board (then event[1] is the key) or "redstone".
mine.lesson.crossing.reopen.hint.2: if event[0] == "mine_device" and event[1] == "treno": close it. elif event[0] == "redstone" and redstone.getInput("left"): open it.
mine.lesson.crossing.trains.goal: Two tracks: a second train can come before the first has passed. Count the trains between the barriers: the crossing opens only when they have all passed. And the Arduino's LED is on (led:1) while the crossing is closed, off (led:0) when it's open.
mine.lesson.crossing.trains.not_yet: Not yet: count the trains and open only when they have all passed; led:1 to the Arduino while closed, led:0 when open.
mine.lesson.crossing.trains.hint.1: A variable trains counts them: +1 for each treno, -1 each time the lever goes on (if trains > 0). Closed means trains > 0.
mine.lesson.crossing.trains.hint.2: A function show() sets the barrier, the light and mine.device.send("led", 1 if closed else 0): call it after every change.
mine.lesson.check.crossing_start: Not yet: when the program starts, the barrier must be open (redstone in front on) and the light off.
mine.lesson.check.crossing: Not yet: after %s the barrier should be %s and the light %s.
mine.lesson.check.crossing_led: Not yet: after %s the board should have got led:%s: led:1 while the barrier is closed, led:0 when it's open.
mine.lesson.farm.title: The farm: rows and fields
mine.lesson.farm.reflection: Byte sowed and harvested a whole field with a few lines, a loop inside a loop. Where do farmers really use machines that follow a program? What would you add to Byte's to make it a better farmer?
mine.lesson.farm.sow.goal: MINE has dug a field in front of Byte: 3 rows of 5 farmland blocks, with water on the left. Byte flies one block above the field (byte.up() first) and sows it all with the wheat seeds in its highlighted slot (byte.placeDown()).
mine.lesson.farm.sow.not_yet: Not yet: every farmland block of the field needs seeds.
mine.lesson.farm.sow.hint.1: A row: 5 times byte.forward() and byte.placeDown(). Then back to the start of the row (5 times byte.back()) and over to the next one: byte.turnRight(), byte.forward(), byte.turnLeft().
mine.lesson.farm.sow.hint.2: A loop inside a loop: for row = 1, 3 do ... the whole row ... end.
mine.lesson.farm.sow.block_hint.1: A row: "repeat 5 times" "move forward", "place a block below". Then "repeat 5 times" "move back", and "turn right", "move forward", "turn left" to the next row.
mine.lesson.farm.sow.block_hint.2: A "repeat 3 times" around all of it: a loop inside a loop. Don't forget "move up" at the start.
mine.lesson.farm.harvest.goal: Now the wheat has grown, but not all of it: some is ripe (golden), some still young (green), in new places every time. Harvest only the ripe wheat (byte.digDown()) and sow again where you harvested.
mine.lesson.farm.harvest.not_yet: Not yet: harvest and sow again all the ripe wheat, and leave the young wheat where it is.
mine.lesson.farm.harvest.hint.1: byte.ripeDown() is true when the wheat under Byte is ripe.
mine.lesson.farm.harvest.hint.2: In the row: byte.forward(), then if byte.ripeDown() then byte.digDown() byte.placeDown() end.
mine.lesson.farm.harvest.block_hint.1: "ripe crop below?" is true when the wheat under Byte is ripe.
mine.lesson.farm.harvest.block_hint.2: In the row: "move forward", then "if" "ripe crop below?": "dig below", "place a block below".
mine.lesson.farm.count.goal: A new field to harvest: this time Byte also says how much ripe wheat it harvested. Count it with a variable: MINE counts it too.
mine.lesson.farm.count.not_yet: Not yet: harvest the ripe wheat, sow again, and make Byte say how many it harvested.
mine.lesson.farm.count.hint.1: Before the loops, local harvested = 0; inside the if, harvested = harvested + 1.
mine.lesson.farm.count.hint.2: At the end, mine.say("I harvested " .. harvested .. " wheat").
mine.lesson.farm.count.block_hint.1: Make a variable "harvested": "set harvested to 0" at the start, "change harvested by 1" inside the "if".
mine.lesson.farm.count.block_hint.2: At the end, "say" with "create text with": "I harvested ", harvested, " wheat".
mine.lesson.check.farm_sown: Not yet: %s of the %s farmland blocks have seeds. Byte flies one block above the field (byte.up() first) and plants with byte.placeDown().
mine.lesson.check.farm_harvest: Not yet: there were %s ripe crops: Byte harvested and planted again %s, and cut %s young ones.
mine.lesson.check.farm_count: Not yet: Byte harvested %s crops, but said %s. Count them with a variable.
mine.lesson.cipher.title: Secret messages: Caesar's cipher
mine.lesson.cipher.reflection: Byte cracked a message without the key, trying them all. Why is Caesar's cipher not safe today? How do the messages on your phone stay secret?
mine.lesson.cipher.caesar.goal: Julius Caesar wrote secret messages moving each letter 3 places forward in the alphabet (A becomes D, Z goes round to C). mine.challenge() gives a new secret message every time: decode it and make Byte say it.
mine.lesson.cipher.caesar.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to say the decoded message.
mine.lesson.cipher.caesar.hint.1: Look at one letter at a time: for i = 1, #secret do local c = secret:sub(i, i) ... end. Spaces stay spaces.
mine.lesson.cipher.caesar.hint.2: string.byte(c) is the letter's number (A is 65). (n - 65 - 3) % 26 + 65 moves it back 3 places, round the alphabet; string.char turns it into a letter again.
mine.lesson.cipher.key.goal: Now the key changes every time: mine.challenge() gives the secret message and the key (how many places each letter was moved). Decode it and make Byte say it.
mine.lesson.cipher.key.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to say the message, decoded with the key MINE gave.
mine.lesson.cipher.key.hint.1: local secret, key = mine.challenge() gives both.
mine.lesson.cipher.key.hint.2: Make the decoding a function, decode(text, key): with the key instead of 3, it works for every key.
mine.lesson.cipher.crack.goal: An intercepted message, and no key! You only know it contains the word BYTE. Try all the keys, from 1 to 25, and make Byte say the message with the right one.
mine.lesson.cipher.crack.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to find the key and say the decoded message.
mine.lesson.cipher.crack.hint.1: for key = 1, 25 do ... end tries them all: decode the message with each one.
mine.lesson.cipher.crack.hint.2: plain:find("BYTE") is true when the decoded message contains BYTE: then say it, and break stops the loop.
mine.lesson.check.cipher_say: Not yet: Byte has to say the decoded message with mine.say.
mine.lesson.check.cipher_wrong: Not yet: the secret message was %s, and Byte said %s. Try decoding the first letter on paper: which way, and how many places?
